contract: One paid order leads to exactly one fulfillment, even when the webhook is delivered concurrently to several worker processes sharing one SQLite database, redelivered after a process restart, or sent under a different event ID; a failed fulfillment is never marked complete and can be retried by another process.

attempts.diagnosis: The handler does SELECT, then awaits fulfillOrder, then writes 'fulfilled'. Nothing is claimed before the await, so every concurrent or overlapping delivery sees no 'fulfilled' row and calls fulfillOrder. Different event IDs for the same order race in the same way.
attempts.changeSummary: Before calling fulfillOrder, the handler now claims the order atomically with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(order_id) DO NOTHING, writing a 'processing' row. Only the delivery with changes === 1 may fulfill; any other delivery returns 'duplicate'. After fulfillOrder succeeds, the row is updated to 'fulfilled'. If fulfillOrder throws, the 'processing' claim is deleted so any process can retry, and the original error is rethrown. No transaction is held across an await. Unknown event types return before any write.

details.summary: Multi-process probes (separate OS processes sharing one SQLite WAL file) for the check-then-await-then-write race in the webhook handler. They cover: the same event delivered concurrently to several processes and repeatedly within one process; different event ids for the same order; a restart duplicate after fulfillment; failure followed by retry from a new process, with no fake acknowledgement and no completed record on failure; a concurrent failure plus success followed by a retry; ignored event types; and independent orders (to catch over-blocking). The original handler should fail the concurrent tests with more than one fulfillment, because the SELECT happens before the awaited fulfillOrder and nothing is claimed.

scenarioTitle: Multi-process payment webhook on SQLite: fulfill each paid order exactly once, across restarts

generatedTests.summary: Multi-process probes (separate OS processes sharing one SQLite WAL file) for the check-then-await-then-write race in the webhook handler. They cover: the same event delivered concurrently to several processes and repeatedly within one process; different event ids for the same order; a restart duplicate after fulfillment; failure followed by retry from a new process, with no fake acknowledgement and no completed record on failure; a concurrent failure plus success followed by a retry; ignored event types; and independent orders (to catch over-blocking). The original handler should fail the concurrent tests with more than one fulfillment, because the SELECT happens before the awaited fulfillOrder and nothing is claimed.
